confirmed.title: New NTIA/steward identifier Error gate floods SPDX SBOMs whose CPE/SWHID identifiers the parser never promotes
confirmed.description: Commit 9cc865a adds NtiaMinimum (and CraOssSteward) to the unique-identifier check and raises it to Error, gating on Identifiers::has_cra_identifier() (purl/cpe/swhid/swid). But the SPDX 2.x parser never populates identifiers.cpe: CPEs arrive as externalRefs with referenceCategory SECURITY / referenceType cpe23Type, and src/parsers/spdx.rs:1016-1022 maps every SECURITY ref to ExternalRefType::Advisories without promoting the CPE (only purl at spdx.rs:939-950 and SWHID at spdx.rs:1008-1015 are promoted; spdx3.rs:465 and cyclonedx.rs:416 do promote CPE). Additionally the SWHID promotion at spdx.rs:1010 requires the exact spelling 'PERSISTENT-ID', so SPDX 2.2 documents using the 2.2 JSON schema's underscore spelling 'PERSISTENT_ID' are not promoted either — even though this same commit explicitly extends EO 14028 to accept SPDX 2.2 (eo14028.rs:24). The same has_cra_identifier() count drives Error-level findings at eo14028.rs:99 and Warning-level at ssdf.rs:159. Verified end-to-end: an SPDX 2.3 SBOM whose two packages each carry a valid cpe23Type ref (and supplier, version, timestamp, DESCRIBES+DEPENDS_ON) → `validate --standard ntia` prints 'Component ... missing unique identifier (PURL/CPE/SWHID/SWID)' per component, Status NON-COMPLIANT, exit 1 — the message itself lists CPE as satisfying. Same flip for --standard oss-steward and eo14028. Underscore-spelled SWHID SPDX 2.2 doc: NON-COMPLIANT; identical doc with hyphen spelling: COMPLIANT.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SPDX 2.3 SBOM identifying every package via cpe23Type externalRefs (common for firmware/medical-device SBOMs that have no purl) → `sbom-tools validate x.spdx.json --standard ntia` → Error SBOM-NTIA-IDENTIFIER per component, verdict NON-COMPLIANT, exit code 1, although the NTIA 'Other Unique Identifiers' element is satisfied by CPE. Same false failure for oss-steward (SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-I-IDENTIFIER Error), eo14028 (SBOM-EO14028-IDENTIFIER Error), and for SPDX 2.2 docs carrying SWHIDs under the schema spelling PERSISTENT_ID.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED end-to-end against the built binary at HEAD (b730c80). (1) An SPDX 2.3 SBOM whose packages carry valid cpe23Type externalRefs (SECURITY category) plus supplier/version/timestamp/DESCRIBES/DEPENDS_ON yields `validate --standard ntia` → Status NON-COMPLIANT, exit 1, with per-component Error 'Component ... missing unique identifier (PURL/CPE/SWHID/SWID)' — the message itself says CPE satisfies the element. (2) --standard oss-steward flips the same way (SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-I-IDENTIFIER Errors, NON-COMPLIANT) and (3) --standard eo14028 reports NON-COMPLIANT with '2/2 components missing unique identifier'. (4) An SPDX doc with SWHIDs under the SPDX 2.2 JSON-schema spelling PERSISTENT_ID is NON-COMPLIANT while the identical doc with PERSISTENT-ID is COMPLIANT. Code root cause verified: model/identifiers.rs:622-624 has_cra_identifier() checks purl/cpe/swhid/swid on ComponentIdentifiers, but src/parsers/spdx.rs:1016 maps every SECURITY external ref to ExternalRefType::Advisories without promoting the CPE into comp.identifiers.cpe (only purl at spdx.rs:939-950 and exact-spelling 'PERSISTENT-ID' swh refs at spdx.rs:1010-1015 are promoted), whereas spdx3.rs:465-466 and cyclonedx.rs:417 do promote CPE — so this is an SPDX 2.x parser gap, not a deliberate decision. The P0 commit 9cc865a made this latent gap verdict-changing by raising the check to Error for NtiaMinimum/CraOssSteward (generic.rs:571-580) and wiring the same predicate into eo14028. Severity high: wrong compliance verdict and wrong exit code on a common real-world SBOM shape (CPE-only firmware/medical-device SBOMs).
verdict.suggested_fix: In src/parsers/spdx.rs convert_package(), inside the external-refs loop (around line 1008-1022): (a) promote CPE refs to first-class identifiers — when ext_ref.reference_type is "cpe23Type" or "cpe22Type" (or the locator starts with "cpe:"), push ext_ref.reference_locator into comp.identifiers.cpe (keep also emitting the Advisories external ref if desired); (b) make the SWHID promotion accept both spellings by normalizing the category, e.g. `ext_ref.reference_category.replace('_', "-") == "PERSISTENT-ID"`, so SPDX 2.2 JSON-schema PERSISTENT_ID documents promote swh refs too. Add regression tests: CPE-only SPDX 2.3 doc is NTIA/oss-steward/eo14028 identifier-compliant; PERSISTENT_ID-spelled SWHID doc matches the hyphen-spelled result.

confirmed.title: SPDX cpe23Type refs (parsed as Advisories) vacuously satisfy the steward Art. 24 vulnerability-handling Error gate and EO 4(g)/CRA 13(6)-(7) disclosure checks
confirmed.description: The reworked steward gate (83d9945) and the new manufacturer_scope_components scoping (shared.rs:14) accept ExternalRefType::Advisories on the primary component as evidence of a vulnerability-handling process / CVD policy / disclosure process. The SPDX parser maps ALL referenceCategory=SECURITY externalRefs — i.e. every cpe23Type/cpe22Type identifier — to ExternalRefType::Advisories (src/parsers/spdx.rs:1016-1022), and additionally copies the first such 'Advisories' locator into document.vulnerability_disclosure_url when the package is described (spdx.rs:788-797), so a bare CPE string like 'cpe:2.3:a:acme:app:1.0:*...' becomes the document's disclosure URL. Consequence: a CPE identifier — which says nothing about security contact or CVD — satisfies the Error-level steward floor (cra.rs:973-1000), the steward CVD-policy Warning (cra.rs:1005-1012), EO 14028 Sec 4(g) (eo14028.rs:189-198), and CRA Art. 13(6)/13(7) (generic.rs:139-176, 265-297). Verified: SPDX SBOM with purls + one cpe23Type ref on the primary, zero security-contact info anywhere → `validate --standard oss-steward` = COMPLIANT (0 errors); removing the CPE ref → NON-COMPLIANT with the Art. 24 Error. Same pair flips the EO 4(g) warning. This is exactly the vacuous-pass class this P0 set intended to close: the manufacturer scoping stops third-party advisories URLs but lets a machine identifier pass an Error gate.
confirmed.failure_scenario: OSS steward publishes an SPDX SBOM where the primary package has a cpe23Type externalRef (standard NVD identification) and no security contact, disclosure URL, or advisories reference exists anywhere → `sbom-tools validate x.spdx.json --standard oss-steward` reports COMPLIANT, exit 0, silently suppressing the CRA Art. 24 vulnerability-handling Error (and `--standard eo14028` suppresses the Sec 4(g) disclosure warning).

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Code reading: src/parsers/spdx.rs:1016-1017 maps ALL referenceCategory=SECURITY externalRefs (including cpe23Type/cpe22Type identifiers) to ExternalRefType::Advisories — spdx.rs contains no CPE handling at all despite the model having identifiers.cpe (src/model/identifiers.rs:458) — and spdx.rs:788-797 copies the first such locator (a bare CPE string) into document.vulnerability_disclosure_url. The steward Art. 24 Error gate (src/quality/compliance/cra.rs:975-984), the 13(7) CVD Warning (cra.rs:1005-1008), EO 4(g) (eo14028.rs:195), and generic 13(6)/13(7) (generic.rs:146,269) all accept Advisories refs on manufacturer-scope components. Empirically reproduced via the real CLI: an SPDX SBOM whose primary package carries only a cpe23Type SECURITY ref and no security-contact info anywhere → `validate --standard oss-steward` = COMPLIANT (0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0); removing the CPE ref → NON-COMPLIANT with the Art. 24 Error + 13(7) Warning. Same pair flips the EO 14028 Sec 4(g) warning (0 warnings with CPE, 1 without). This is not a documented/deliberate decision — commit 83d9945 explicitly targeted vacuous CRA passes, and the violation message text says the remedy is a SecurityContact/Advisories reference, so a machine identifier passing the Error gate is exactly the class this work meant to close.
verdict.suggested_fix: Fix at the parser layer (src/parsers/spdx.rs): in the externalRefs mapping (~line 1016), stop treating every SECURITY ref as Advisories — promote reference_type cpe22Type/cpe23Type into the component's CPE identifier (comp.identifiers.cpe.push(locator), mirroring the existing SWHID promotion at lines 1010-1014, with `continue`), map SECURITY reference_type "advisory"/"fix"/"url" to ExternalRefType::Advisories, and anything else in SECURITY to ExternalRefType::Other(reference_type). Additionally harden the disclosure-URL copy at spdx.rs:788-797 to only accept locators that are URL-shaped (starts_with "http://"/"https://"/"mailto:"), so a non-URL locator can never become document.vulnerability_disclosure_url. Add a regression test: SPDX fixture with cpe23Type-only SECURITY ref must fail oss-steward Art. 24 and raise the EO 4(g) warning.

confirmed.title: known_value() rejects genuine component names 'none'/'unknown' as placeholders, failing legitimate SBOMs with an Error at every level
confirmed.description: known_value() treats NOASSERTION/NONE/UNKNOWN (case-insensitive) as absent, and generic.rs:500 now applies it to component NAMES at Error severity for ALL levels (likewise eo14028.rs:119 counts them as nameless). The sentinel convention is an SPDX field convention (supplier, downloadLocation, licenses); it is not defined for package names, and CycloneDX has no NOASSERTION/NONE convention at all. Real packages with these names exist: npm 'none' (pkg:npm/none) and npm 'unknown'. Verified: a CycloneDX SBOM containing component {name:'none', version:'1.0.0', purl:'pkg:npm/none@1.0.0', author set} → `validate --standard ntia` reports Error SBOM-NTIA-NAME 'Component must have a name', Status NON-COMPLIANT, exit 1. The same known_value is fine for supplier/author/version placeholders; the defect is applying full sentinel semantics to the name field regardless of source format. A narrower rule (empty/whitespace, or sentinels only for SPDX-sourced fields where the spec defines them) avoids the false verdict.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SBOM (any format) whose dependency tree includes the published npm package 'none' or 'unknown', fully identified with purl/version/author → NtiaMinimum/EO14028/FDA/CRA all report a gating 'Component must have a name' Error → verdict NON-COMPLIANT, exit 1, for a fully compliant SBOM.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed, not refuted. (1) shared.rs:52-62 known_value() rejects 'none'/'unknown'/'noassertion' case-insensitively; generic.rs:500 applies it to comp.name for ALL compliance levels at Error severity, and eo14028.rs:119 counts such components as nameless. (2) Reproduced via the real CLI: a CycloneDX SBOM with component {name:'none', version:'1.0.0', purl:'pkg:npm/none@1.0.0', author, supplier} run through `validate --standard ntia` emits Error SBOM-NTIA-NAME 'Component must have a name' on element pkg:npm/none@1.0.0, Status NON-COMPLIANT, exit code 1. (3) The scenario is real: registry.npmjs.org/none and registry.npmjs.org/unknown both return HTTP 200 — published packages with these exact names exist, so ordinary dependency trees can contain them. (4) The 'deliberate decision' defense fails: the generic.rs:497-499 comment documents blocking placeholders on the premise these strings are always placeholders; SPDX defines NONE/NOASSERTION sentinels only for specific fields (downloadLocation, license, supplier, copyright), not package name, and CycloneDX defines no sentinel convention at all — so a fully-corroborated genuine name being failed is an unconsidered false-positive class, not a documented tradeoff. Wrong compliance verdict (NON-COMPLIANT, exit 1) for a compliant SBOM = high per the rubric, though low frequency.
verdict.suggested_fix: Add a name-specific gate in src/quality/compliance/shared.rs, e.g. `known_name(comp: &Component) -> bool`: reject empty/whitespace and NOASSERTION unconditionally, but accept 'none'/'unknown' when corroborated by a unique identifier — the component has a purl whose name segment equals comp.name case-insensitively (pkg:npm/none@1.0.0 corroborates 'none'). Replace `known_value(Some(comp.name.as_str()))` with this gate at src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:500 and src/quality/compliance/eo14028.rs:119. This preserves the anti-vacuous-pass hardening (generator-emitted placeholder names essentially never ship with a matching purl) while eliminating the false NON-COMPLIANT for genuinely named packages.

confirmed.title: has_support_lifecycle_evidence(): substring match 'eol' on any component property name falsely satisfies the FDA level-of-support and CRA 13(11) elements
confirmed.description: The helper returns true if ANY component has ANY property whose lowercased name merely CONTAINS 'eol' (or 'lifecycle'), ignoring the property VALUE entirely. 'geolocation' contains 'eol' (g-e-o-l...), as do 'geology', 'aeolian', etc. Verified: adding property {name:'geolocation', value:'enabled'} to a single third-party dependency suppresses the new FDA warning 'no level-of-support or end-of-support information found' (SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT, generic.rs:403-416) — 3 warnings without the property, 2 with it. Two additional weaknesses compound it: (a) evidence from any single component satisfies a requirement the FDA guidance states per component ('each component's level of support'), including upstream registry metadata on a dependency, contradicting the manufacturer-scoping philosophy applied elsewhere in this same diff; (b) a property named e.g. 'lifecycle' with an empty or 'unknown' value still counts (no known_value() applied). Same helper gates the CRA Art. 13(11) Info at generic.rs:303.
confirmed.failure_scenario: FDA premarket SBOM with no support/EOL information anywhere, but one dependency carries a copied upstream property named 'geolocation' (or any name containing 'eol') → `validate --standard fda` omits the FD&C §524B level-of-support warning, and with --fail-on-warning the SBOM exits 0 instead of 2.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED. src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:482-490: has_support_lifecycle_evidence() accepts ANY component property whose lowercased name contains the substring "eol" (line 487) or "lifecycle", ignoring the property value entirely (no known_value() gate). Verified end-to-end: a CycloneDX SBOM with zero support/EOL data produces the SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT warning under `validate --standard fda`; adding {name:"geolocation", value:"enabled"} to one dependency suppresses it (warning count 2 -> 1 in an otherwise-clean SBOM). The same helper gates the CRA Art. 13(11) Info at line 303, so that is suppressed too. Compounding weaknesses (a) any-single-component evidence and (b) no value check are also as claimed. One caveat: the claimed exit-code flip (0 vs 2 with --fail-on-warning) is not currently reachable, because the CycloneDX parser (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:280-310) only emits Tool/Person creators, so the FDA "manufacturer (organization) as creator" warning (generic.rs:350-366) always co-fires on CycloneDX inputs and keeps exit 2; SPDX inputs have Organization creators but the SPDX parser never populates component properties, so the bogus-property path is CycloneDX-only. The core defect (false evidence suppressing a required-element warning, misleading report output) is real and reachable via the CLI; severity medium (misleading output, warning-level check) rather than a hard verdict flip in the current parser state.
verdict.suggested_fix: In has_support_lifecycle_evidence() (src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:482-490), (1) match property names on tokens, not substrings: split name_lower on non-alphanumeric chars and accept only exact tokens "eol"/"lifecycle", plus explicit phrases "end-of-life"/"end-of-support"/"endoflife"/"endofsupport"; (2) require a meaningful value: `&& known_value(Some(p.value.as_str())).is_some()`. E.g.: `let is_lifecycle_name = name_lower.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()).any(|t| t == "eol" || t == "lifecycle") || name_lower.contains("end-of-life") || name_lower.contains("end-of-support") || name_lower.contains("endoflife") || name_lower.contains("endofsupport"); is_lifecycle_name && known_value(Some(p.value.as_str())).is_some()`. Optionally (follow-up, matches FDA "each component" wording and the diff's manufacturer-scoping philosophy): require the evidence on the primary/root component or on all components rather than any single one.

confirmed.title: Primary-participation warning fires on spec-conformant CycloneDX SBOMs whose root is explicitly declared with an empty dependsOn
confirmed.description: The new graph-participation check warns when the primary component appears in no edge. The CycloneDX parser (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:184-219) creates edges only from non-empty dependsOn/provides lists, so a dependencies entry {"ref":"root"} with empty dependsOn — the CycloneDX-specified way to positively assert 'this component has no dependencies' ('components that do not have their own dependencies MUST be declared as empty elements') — is indistinguishable from the root being absent from the graph. Verified: CycloneDX SBOM with metadata.component 'acme-image', dependencies [{ref:'img',dependsOn:[]},{ref:'a@1',dependsOn:['b@1']}] → `validate --standard ntia` warns "Primary component 'acme-image' participates in no dependency relationship" (SBOM-NTIA-DEPENDENCY), and with --fail-on-warning exits 2. This shape is normal for container/firmware SBOMs where contents are compositions rather than dependsOn edges. The parser would need to record explicitly-declared-empty roots (or the check should skip roots present in the dependencies array) to avoid flagging complete declarations.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Container-image CycloneDX SBOM that declares the root in the dependencies array with dependsOn: [] (explicit, complete declaration per spec) → NTIA/FDA/CRA/steward runs emit a 'participates in no dependency relationship' warning; CI running `validate --fail-on-warning` fails with exit 2 on a conformant SBOM.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed, not refuted. (1) Parser: src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:184-219 builds edges only by iterating dep.depends_on.unwrap_or_default(); a dependencies entry {"ref":"img","dependsOn":[]} produces no edge and no other model trace, so the explicitly-declared-empty root is indistinguishable from a root absent from the dependencies array. Compositions (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:324-338) only set the completeness declaration and never create containment edges, so container-style SBOMs get no root edges either way. (2) Check: src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:862-878 warns whenever the primary component id appears in no edge and edges exist among >1 components. (3) Reproduced with the actual binary: CycloneDX SBOM with metadata.component 'acme-image' (bom-ref img), components liba/libb, dependencies [{ref:'img',dependsOn:[]},{ref:'a@1',dependsOn:['b@1']}] -> `validate --standard ntia` emits "[WARN] Primary component 'acme-image' participates in no dependency relationship" (rule SBOM-NTIA-DEPENDENCY), and `--fail-on-warning` exits 2. (4) The input is spec-conformant: CycloneDX requires components without dependencies to be declared as empty elements in the dependency graph, so the empty entry is a complete, positive assertion, and the check's rationale comment ("no declared relationships") is factually wrong for this shape. No comment or test in the P0 diff documents treating explicit-empty as missing, so it is not a deliberate decision. Severity is medium: warning-level (status stays COMPLIANT), but flips the documented exit-code contract to 2 under --fail-on-warning in CI on conformant SBOMs.
verdict.suggested_fix: Preserve the explicit-empty declaration through the model and honor it in the check. Minimal version: (a) add a field to NormalizedSbom, e.g. `pub explicit_no_dependency_ids: HashSet<CanonicalId>` (src/model/sbom.rs); (b) in src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:184-219, when a dependencies entry resolves via id_map and its depends_on is None or empty, insert the resolved id into that set (also reasonable: insert every dep.ref_field that resolves, since any presence in the dependencies array is an assertion about that component's dependencies); (c) in src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:862-878, skip the primary-participation warning when `sbom.explicit_no_dependency_ids.contains(primary_id)`. Optionally extend the orphan-ratio check at generic.rs:889-894 to exclude ids in the same set, and mirror for SPDX NONE-dependency relationships later.

confirmed.title: Any single eucc_* sidecar field — even an expired date or empty string — suppresses the Critical-class Annex IV EUCC gate
confirmed.description: check_class_eucc_reference (cra.rs:628-633) and the conformity summary's eucc_present (cra.rs:50-54) treat `is_some()` on ANY one of the four eucc_* sidecar fields as satisfying EUCC evidence. There is no expiry check on eucc_valid_until and no empty-string guard on the String fields. This contradicts the dedicated EUCC profile in the same codebase (eucc.rs:26/42/58 guards `!s.is_empty()`; eucc.rs:84-97 makes an expired eucc_valid_until an Error) and the branch's own shared placeholder-gate principle from 9cc865a (empty values must not satisfy required-element gates). Verified via CLI: `validate --standard cra --cra-sidecar {productClass: critical, euccValidUntil: 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z}` produces NO SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-IV violation, while the control sidecar `{productClass: critical}` produces the Error '[CRA Annex IV / EUCC] Product class Critical requires...'. Same suppression verified with `euccProtectionProfileId: ""`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Manufacturer of an Annex IV Critical product runs `sbom-tools validate sbom.json --standard cra --cra-sidecar side.json` where side.json pins productClass critical and carries only a 2020 (expired) euccValidUntil, or an empty-string euccProtectionProfileId from a template scaffold. The Error-severity SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-IV violation is suppressed; on an otherwise-clean SBOM error_count drops to 0 and the exit code flips from COMPLIANCE_ERRORS(1) to SUCCESS(0) — a false compliance pass for the strictest CRA class, while `--standard eucc` on the same sidecar reports the certificate as expired at Error severity.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED. Code inspection: cra.rs:628-633 (check_class_eucc_reference) and cra.rs:50-54 (conformity summary eucc_present) gate the Critical-class Annex IV EUCC requirement on bare `is_some()` for all four eucc_* sidecar fields, with no empty-string guard (eucc_protection_profile_id/eucc_target_of_evaluation/eucc_itsef_identifier are Option<String>) and no expiry check (eucc_valid_until is Option<DateTime<Utc>>). The same P0 diff's dedicated EUCC profile contradicts this: eucc.rs:26/42/58 require `!s.is_empty()` and eucc.rs:84-97 make an expired eucc_valid_until an Error. Dispatch (context.rs:128-152) shows --standard cra runs only check_cra -> check_class_eucc_reference (cra.rs:574); check_eucc_substantial runs only under the separate EuccSubstantial level, so nothing compensates under CRA. CLI reproduction with target/debug/sbom-tools validate tests/fixtures/cra/cra-compliant.cdx.json --standard cra: sidecar {"productClass":"critical"} yields 3 errors including the SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-IV Error; adding only "euccValidUntil":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z" (expired) or only "euccProtectionProfileId":"" drops it to 2 errors with the Annex IV Error suppressed. On an otherwise-clean SBOM this flips error_count 1->0 and the process exit code 1->0 — a false compliance pass for the strictest CRA class, while --standard eucc on the same sidecar would report the certificate expired at Error severity. The cra.rs:626 comment documents sidecar authority over URL scanning, not acceptance of expired/empty values; the branch's own placeholder-gate principle (9cc865a) and eucc.rs guards (83d9945) establish the opposite convention, so this is an inconsistency, not a deliberate decision.
verdict.suggested_fix: In src/quality/compliance/cra.rs, replace both bare is_some() blocks (cra.rs:628-633 and cra.rs:50-54) with value-validating gates matching eucc.rs semantics — ideally via a shared helper on CraSidecar (src/model/cra_sidecar.rs), e.g. `pub fn has_live_eucc_evidence(&self) -> bool { self.eucc_protection_profile_id.as_deref().is_some_and(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()) || self.eucc_target_of_evaluation.as_deref().is_some_and(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()) || self.eucc_itsef_identifier.as_deref().is_some_and(|s| !s.trim().is_empty()) || self.eucc_valid_until.is_some_and(|d| d > chrono::Utc::now()) }`, and use it in check_class_eucc_reference and build_conformity_summary. Add a regression test asserting SBOM-CRA-ANNEX-IV still fires for a Critical-class sidecar carrying only an expired euccValidUntil or an empty-string euccProtectionProfileId.

confirmed.title: manufacturer_scope_components returns empty for cyclic dependency graphs, making manufacturer evidence unsatisfiable and firing a false steward Error
confirmed.description: When primary_component_id is unset and every component has at least one incoming edge (mutually-depending components / a graph that is a union of cycles), the root fallback at shared.rs:22-30 yields an empty Vec. All five consumers then treat component-level evidence as absent regardless of what refs exist: steward vuln-handling (cra.rs:975, Error), steward CVD (cra.rs:1005, Warning), Art. 13(6) contact (generic.rs:140, Warning), Art. 13(7) CVD (generic.rs:266, Warning), EO14028 4(g) (eo14028.rs:191, Warning). Verified via CLI: a CycloneDX SBOM with components liba/libb, dependencies a→b AND b→a, no metadata.component, where liba carries BOTH security-contact and advisories external refs, run with `validate --standard oss-steward` yields '[CRA Art. 24 / Annex I Part II] OSS steward must operate a vulnerability-handling process' at Error, is_compliant=false, exit code 1. The pre-83d9945 code (components.values().any) passed this SBOM.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An OSS steward SBOM without metadata.component whose declared dependencies form a cycle covering all components (mutual/circular deps are legal in CycloneDX and occur in real npm/maven graphs) but which correctly declares SecurityContact + Advisories refs → validate --standard oss-steward exits 1 with a false Error-severity Art. 24 violation; the SBOM was compliant before the commit and per the regulation.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, not refuted — reproduced end-to-end through the real CLI.

Code: src/quality/compliance/shared.rs:14-31. When `primary_component_id` is unset, the fallback collects components with no incoming dependency edge (lines 22-30). In a graph where every component has at least one incoming edge (mutual/circular deps, legal in CycloneDX), the filter yields an empty Vec. Nothing handles the empty case, and the doc comment (lines 5-13) documents only the "root components" intent, not a deliberate fail-on-cycles decision.

Reproduction: wrote a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM (scratchpad/cyclic.cdx.json) with components liba/libb, dependencies liba→libb AND libb→liba, no metadata.component, liba carrying BOTH `security-contact` and `advisories` external references (parser maps these at src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:484). `cargo run -- validate --standard oss-steward cyclic.cdx.json` → "Status: NON-COMPLIANT (1 errors, 1 warnings)": Error "[CRA Art. 24 / Annex I Part II] OSS steward must operate a vulnerability-handling process" (cra.rs:989-1000) plus Warning "[CRA Art. 13(7)]" (cra.rs:1013), exit code 1.

Cause isolation: removing only the libb→liba edge (same refs, same components) → "Status: COMPLIANT (0 errors, 0 warnings)", exit 0. The cycle alone flips the verdict.

Regression check: `git show 83d9945^:src/quality/compliance/cra.rs` lines 944-952 show the pre-P0 code used `sbom.components.values().any(...)`, which passes this SBOM. So the P0 diff introduced a false Error-severity non-compliance on a previously (and per-regulation) compliant SBOM. The same empty scope also silently disables the four Warning-level consumers (cra.rs:1005, generic.rs:140, generic.rs:266, eo14028.rs:191).

Severity: high — wrong compliance verdict and wrong exit code through a real CLI path.

confirmed.title: Primary-component short-circuit excludes sibling described products — false 13(6)/13(7) findings on multi-product SPDX SBOMs
confirmed.description: When primary_component_id is set, manufacturer_scope_components returns ONLY that one component (shared.rs:15-21). The SPDX parser sets the primary to the FIRST DESCRIBES target only (spdx.rs:782-785), so in an SPDX document describing multiple products of the same manufacturer, security refs on the second and later described products no longer count as manufacturer evidence (and the parser's doc-level vulnerability_disclosure_url harvest at spdx.rs:788-796 also only reads the first). Verified via CLI: SPDX-2.3 SBOM with SPDXRef-DOCUMENT DESCRIBES SPDXRef-A and SPDXRef-B, where product-b carries the SECURITY/advisory external ref (https://acme.example/security/advisories) → `validate --standard cra` emits Warnings '[CRA Art. 13(6)] SBOM should include a security contact...' and '[CRA Art. 13(7)] SBOM should reference a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A vendor suite SBOM (SPDX documentDescribes lists several first-party products; advisories URL attached to one that is not first in the relationships array) run as `validate --standard cra --fail-on-warning` exits COMPLIANCE_WARNINGS(2) instead of 0 — false non-compliance on the manufacturer's own evidence. Fix direction: include all DESCRIBES targets / all roots alongside the primary, not just the first.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED via code reading and live CLI reproduction. shared.rs:14-21 returns only the primary component when primary_component_id is set, and spdx.rs:777-785 sets the primary from only the FIRST document DESCRIBES relationship (guarded by `sbom.primary_component_id.is_none()`); the doc-level vulnerability_disclosure_url harvest at spdx.rs:788-796 is inside that same first-target-only block. Reproduced end-to-end: an SPDX-2.3 SBOM with `SPDXRef-DOCUMENT DESCRIBES SPDXRef-A` then `DESCRIBES SPDXRef-B`, where product-b carries the SECURITY/advisory externalRef (mapped to ExternalRefType::Advisories at spdx.rs:1017), yields `validate --standard cra` warnings "[CRA Art. 13(6)] SBOM should include a security contact..." (generic.rs:139-176, rule SBOM-CRA-ART-13-6-CONTACT) and "[CRA Art. 13(7)] SBOM should reference a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy" (generic.rs:265-296, rule SBOM-CRA-ART-13-7). Swapping only the order of the two DESCRIBES relationships (identical semantics — SPDX relationship arrays are unordered) removes both warnings (4→2 warnings on the raw fixture, 3→1 on a PURL-complete fixture). With --fail-on-warning this warning is what drives exit 2 on an otherwise warning-free vendor SBOM. Not a deliberate decision: commit 83d9945's stated scope is "primary/root components" (plural), and sibling DESCRIBES targets are roots (no incoming dependency edges) belonging to the manufacturer — the short-circuit excludes exactly the components the scoping rationale (rejecting third-party dependencies' upstream refs) says should count. Severity: medium-to-high — false non-compliance findings and order-dependent verdicts on multi-product SBOMs, flipping CI exit code under --fail-on-warning.
verdict.suggested_fix: Two coordinated minimal changes: (1) In src/parsers/spdx.rs, record ALL document DESCRIBES targets, not just the first — e.g., add a `described_component_ids: Vec<CanonicalId>` (or reuse existing roots metadata) on NormalizedSbom, push every resolved DESCRIBES target into it, keep the first as primary_component_id, and move the advisories-URL harvest (spdx.rs:788-796) out of the `is_none()` guard so any described component's Advisories ref can populate document.vulnerability_disclosure_url. (2) In src/quality/compliance/shared.rs manufacturer_scope_components, when primary is set return the primary PLUS all described components (union, deduped) instead of `vec![primary]`; fall back to root components (no incoming edge) only when neither primary nor described ids exist. This keeps the anti-vacuous-pass property (dependency components' upstream refs still never count, even in edge-less SBOMs) while making sibling first-party products' security/advisories refs satisfy Art. 13(6)/13(7). Add a regression test asserting the CRA verdict is invariant under DESCRIBES relationship reordering.

confirmed.title: Compound algorithmFamily strings ("DES-CBC", "AES-128-CBC", "3DES-EDE-CBC") classify as Unknown, turning required CNSA2/PQC Errors into Warnings — false compliance pass
confirmed.description: classify_token only tries (a) a whole-token alias lookup, (b) one rsplit at the last '-' requiring an all-digit suffix, and (c) a trailing digit run. A family string carrying a mode or scheme suffix ("DES-CBC", "AES-128-CBC", "3DES-EDE-CBC", "AES-256-GCM") fails all three, and the name fallback in classify_algorithm (src/model/crypto.rs:1495) is explicitly gated on family.is_none(), so a declared-but-compound family blocks the token scan that would have recognized it (classify_algorithm_names parses all of these correctly). The CycloneDX parser passes algorithmFamily through verbatim as a free string (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:697), so these spellings are fully reachable. Result: the asset lands in AlgorithmClass::Unknown, producing only SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN / no PQC violation, and is_compliant (mod.rs: error_count == 0) stays true. Fix direction: when the declared family fails classify_token, run classify_algorithm_names over the family string (picking the most severe class) before giving up.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM with one cryptographic-asset: assetType=algorithm, algorithmProperties.algorithmFamily="DES-CBC" (or "AES-128-CBC"). `ComplianceChecker::new(Cnsa2).check()` and `new(NistPqc).check()` both return is_compliant=true with only a Warning — verified empirically. DES must be an SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005/SBOM-PQC-005 Error and AES-128 an SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-001 Error; both broken/disallowed algorithms pass CNSA 2.0 and NIST PQC readiness.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED empirically via the real CLI path, not just code reading.

Code mechanics match the claim exactly:
- classify_token (src/model/crypto.rs:1204-1247) tries only (a) whole-token alias_lookup, (b) one rsplit_once('-') requiring an all-digit suffix, (c) a trailing digit run. "DES-CBC" fails all three ("CBC" is not digits, no trailing digit run); same for "AES-128-CBC" and "3DES-EDE-CBC" (alias table at crypto.rs:1119-1120 has "3DES-EDE" but not the -CBC form).
- classify_algorithm (crypto.rs:1452-1501): a declared-but-unrecognized family falls through to OID (absent), elliptic_curve (absent), then the name fallback at crypto.rs:1495 is gated on `family.is_none() && oid.is_none()`, so the declared compound family blocks the token scan that parses these strings correctly (classify_algorithm_names, crypto.rs:1259). Result: AlgorithmClass::Unknown.
- Parser passes algorithmFamily through verbatim (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:697), so the input is fully reachable.
- Unknown class hits CnsaVerdict::Unknown → Warning SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN only (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:385-408); is_compliant is error_count==0.

Empirical runs (cargo run -- validate, JSON output):
1. CBOM with cryptographic-asset algorithmFamily="DES-CBC", --standard cnsa2 → is_compliant: true, error_count: 0, one Warning: "'legacy-cipher' cannot be classified (no recognizable algorithm family, OID, or name)" — message is even self-contradictory since a family WAS declared.
2. Same file, --standard pqc → is_compliant: true, only Warning "'legacy-cipher' missing nistQuantumSecurityLevel field" — DES sails through NIST PQC readiness with no SBOM-PQC-005.
3. algorithmFamily="AES-128-CBC", --standard cnsa2 → is_compliant: true, error_count: 0, same unclassifiable Warning (should be SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-001 Error: CNSA 2.0 requires AES-256).
4. Control: algorithmFamily="DES" (plain) → is_compliant: false, Error "'legacy-cipher' uses DES, a broken legacy algorithm not permitted by CNSA 2.0" — proving the intended behavior that the compound spelling silently escapes.

This is a wrong compliance verdict (false pass) for broken/disallowed algorithms under both CNSA2 and NIST-PQC — high severity. Nothing in the doc comments frames compound family strings as deliberately unsupported; the name-fallback gate is documented as bounding false positives on component NAMES, not as a reason to skip scanning the declared family string itself.
verdict.suggested_fix: In classify_algorithm (src/model/crypto.rs), after the whole-family classify_token attempt and the family-declared-but-unrecognized OID retry (after line 1483), add a last-resort scan of the declared family string itself before falling through to Unknown: run classify_algorithm_names(f) over the trimmed family and, if non-empty, return fill_parameter on the most severe classification (order Broken > ClassicalQuantumVulnerable > others, e.g. via a small severity rank over AlgorithmClass, or min_by_key on a rank function) so "AES-128-CBC" yields AES-128 and "DES-CBC"/"3DES-EDE-CBC" yield the broken family. Keeping it after the OID retry preserves the documented authority order (recognized family token > OID > family token-scan > curve > name). Add unit tests for "DES-CBC", "3DES-EDE-CBC", "AES-128-CBC", "AES-256-GCM" asserting Broken/Broken/Symmetric-128/Symmetric-256, plus a compliance-level test that a CBOM asset with algorithmFamily="DES-CBC" fails Cnsa2 and NistPqc with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005 / SBOM-PQC-005 Errors.

confirmed.title: Truncated SHA-2 variants (SHA-512/256, SHA-512/224) classify as full SHA-512 and are falsely CNSA 2.0 Approved
confirmed.description: normalize_algo_token maps '/' to '-', so "SHA-512/256" becomes "SHA-512-256". In classify_token's rsplit branch, alias_lookup("SHA-512") returns ("SHA-2", Some("512")), and the merge `param.map(str::to_string).or_else(|| Some(digits.to_string()))` prefers the alias-implied parameter (512) over the explicit trailing digits (256). The asset is classified as SHA-2/512, which cnsa2_verdict approves (crypto.rs:129). The OID path handles the same algorithms correctly (2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.5/.6 → 224/256, which correctly produce SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-002 Errors), so the family-string and OID paths give opposite verdicts for the identical algorithm. SHA-512/256 (256-bit digest) is not on the CNSA 2.0 hash allowlist.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM algorithm asset with algorithmFamily="SHA-512/256": CNSA2 check returns is_compliant=true with ZERO violations (verified), while the same algorithm declared via OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.6 returns is_compliant=false with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-002. Label() also reports it as "SHA-512" in all messages.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED empirically. I compiled and ran a throwaway integration test calling the public API `sbom_tools::model::classify_algorithm`: (1) `classify_algorithm(Some("SHA-512/256"), None, None, None, None)` returns family="SHA-2", parameter="512", label "SHA-512"; (2) the same algorithm via OID `2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.6` returns parameter="256". Code path matches the claim exactly: normalize_algo_token (src/model/crypto.rs:1181-1189) maps '/' to '-', so "SHA-512/256" -> "SHA-512-256"; direct alias_lookup misses; the rsplit branch (crypto.rs:1221-1230) splits into base="SHA-512"/digits="256", alias_lookup("SHA-512") yields ("SHA-2", Some("512")) (crypto.rs:1157), and the merge at crypto.rs:1226-1228 (`param.map(str::to_string).or_else(|| Some(digits.to_string()))`) lets the alias-implied 512 win over the explicit trailing 256. cnsa2_verdict (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:128-129) then hits `Some(384 | 512) => CnsaVerdict::Approved`, so a CBOM asset with algorithmFamily="SHA-512/256" (a 256-bit digest, not on the CNSA 2.0 hash allowlist) passes CNSA2 with zero violations, while the identical algorithm declared by OID is correctly rejected with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-002 (OID table at crypto.rs:1326-1327 maps .5/.6 to 224/256). The two declaration paths give opposite compliance verdicts for the same algorithm — a wrong compliance verdict (high severity per the review rubric). SHA-512/224 fails identically. label() also misreports it as "SHA-512". This is not a documented/deliberate decision anywhere in the P0 diff.
verdict.suggested_fix: Minimal, zero-risk fix: add explicit alias entries for the FIPS 180-4 truncated variants in alias_lookup (src/model/crypto.rs, after line 1157), since normalize_algo_token already folds '/' to '-': `"SHA-512-256" | "SHA512-256" => ("SHA-2", Some("256")), "SHA-512-224" | "SHA512-224" => ("SHA-2", Some("224")),`. These then hit the direct-alias branch at classify_token:1216 before the faulty rsplit merge is reached, aligning the family-string path with the OID path. (Alternative broader fix: in the rsplit branch at crypto.rs:1226-1228, prefer the explicit trailing digits over the alias-implied parameter — `let param = Some(digits.to_string());` — but the alias-table entries are the smallest change with no risk to other token shapes.) Add a regression test asserting classify_algorithm(Some("SHA-512/256"),...) yields parameter "256" and that cnsa2 flags it with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-002.

confirmed.title: Name/ref fallback takes the FIRST recognized token instead of the most severe — hash-first names like "sha384-rsa-signature" hide the quantum-vulnerable RSA and pass both standards
confirmed.description: classify_algorithm step 4 uses `classify_algorithm_names(n).into_iter().next()`, and classify_bom_ref (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:64-67) does the same on raw ref strings. classify_algorithm_names returns mentions in token order, so whichever algorithm token appears first wins. For a signature-algorithm asset (or certificate signatureAlgorithmRef string) whose name puts the digest first — "sha384-rsa-signature", "SHA384-RSA", "sha512-ecdsa-p384" — the classification is SHA-2/384 (CNSA Approved, PQC clean) and the RSA/ECDSA identity is discarded. The cipher-suite path correctly iterates ALL classifications (crypto.rs:496); only these two single-pick paths are wrong. Fix: pick the worst class (Broken > ClassicalQuantumVulnerable > not-approved > …) among all mentions.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM algorithm asset named "sha384-rsa-signature" with no algorithmFamily/OID (typical CycloneDX 1.6): CNSA2 → is_compliant=true, zero errors; NistPqc → is_compliant=true (verified). Renaming it "rsa-sha384-signature" correctly yields SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-006 and SBOM-PQC-001 Errors. Same false pass for cert signatureAlgorithmRef strings like "sha384-rsa-signer".

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by code reading and end-to-end CLI reproduction. classify_algorithm step 4 (src/model/crypto.rs:1498) and the classify_bom_ref raw-string fallback (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:64-67) both take `.into_iter().next()` on classify_algorithm_names, which returns mentions in token order (src/model/crypto.rs:1266-1296). alias_lookup has no composite "SHA384-RSA" entry, so "sha384-rsa-signature" yields [SHA-2/384, RSA] and the RSA mention is discarded. Ran the real binary: `validate --standard cnsa2` and `--standard pqc` on a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM algorithm asset named "sha384-rsa-signature" (no algorithmFamily/OID) both report COMPLIANT with zero errors; renaming the same asset "rsa-sha384-signature" produces NON-COMPLIANT with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-006 and the IR 8547 quantum-vulnerable error. The cipher-suite path (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:496, 879) iterates ALL classifications, so the single-pick behavior is an inconsistency, not a documented design decision. Severity high: wrong compliance verdict reachable via the validate CLI.
verdict.suggested_fix: Pick the most severe mention instead of the first. Add a severity ranking for AlgorithmClass (e.g. Broken=5 > ClassicalQuantumVulnerable=4 > Unknown=3 > Symmetric/Hash/other non-PQC=2 > PQC-approved=1) and replace `.into_iter().next()` with `.into_iter().max_by_key(|c| class_severity(c.class))` in both src/model/crypto.rs:1498 (classify_algorithm step 4, keeping fill_parameter) and src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:64-67 (classify_bom_ref raw-ref fallback). Add regression tests asserting "sha384-rsa-signature" and "rsa-sha384-signature" classify identically (RSA, ClassicalQuantumVulnerable) and that both fail CNSA2 (SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-006) and NIST PQC (SBOM-PQC-001).

confirmed.title: Certificate branch silently accepts Unknown signature-algorithm classifications while counting the cert as 'evaluated' — certificate-only CBOM passes CNSA2 and PQC vacuously
confirmed.description: In check_cnsa2 (line 256-276) and check_nist_pqc (line 574-601), a certificate with a signature_algorithm_ref increments crypto_assets_evaluated and then only acts on NotApproved/Broken/ClassicalQuantumVulnerable classifications. CnsaVerdict::Unknown (dangling ref, ref resolving to a non-algorithm component such as the key or the cert itself, or an unclassifiable target) produces no violation at all — unlike the algorithm branch, which emits SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN. This directly contradicts classify_bom_ref's own doc comment (line 53: 'opaque refs like "sig-algo-42" classify as Unknown rather than silently passing checks') and re-opens exactly the vacuous-pass class commit 7a1c9c2 claims to close: the ref satisfies the CNSA2-000/PQC-000 inventory gate while nothing was actually verified.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM containing only one cryptographic-asset certificate with certificateProperties.signatureAlgorithmRef="sig-algo-42" (dangling), or a ref pointing at a related-crypto-material component: both Cnsa2 and NistPqc checks return is_compliant=true with ZERO violations (verified for both variants) — a false 'CNSA 2.0 compliant' claim backed by no evaluated algorithm.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by code reading and by running the real CLI. `cargo run -- validate --standard cnsa2,pqc` on a CBOM containing only a cryptographic-asset certificate with certificateProperties.signatureAlgorithmRef="sig-algo-42" (dangling) reports "COMPLIANT (0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info)" for both CNSA 2.0 and NIST PQC Readiness, exit 0. Mechanism: in check_cnsa2 (src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:256-276) and check_nist_pqc (crypto.rs:574-601), the certificate branch increments crypto_assets_evaluated unconditionally once a signature_algorithm_ref is present, then only reacts to NotApproved (CNSA2) or Broken/ClassicalQuantumVulnerable (PQC); an Unknown classification produces no violation and no warning. This contradicts three explicit contracts in the same file: CnsaVerdict::Unknown's doc "cannot verify (Warning, never a silent pass)" (crypto.rs:32), classify_bom_ref's doc "opaque refs like \"sig-algo-42\" classify as Unknown rather than silently passing checks" (crypto.rs:53), and the gate comment "an inventory of unevaluable assets cannot satisfy the CNSA2-000 gate" (crypto.rs:235-236). The algorithm branch handles the identical situation by emitting SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN (crypto.rs:385-408). Verdict impact is real: without the bogus count the SBOM would hit CNSA2-000/PQC-000 Errors and be NON-COMPLIANT (is_compliant = error_count == 0, mod.rs:635); instead it passes cleanly. Claim confirmed, not refuted.
verdict.suggested_fix: In the certificate branches, handle the Unknown outcome explicitly, mirroring the algorithm branch. In check_cnsa2 (crypto.rs:261) replace the `if let CnsaVerdict::NotApproved` with a full match: NotApproved -> existing SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-001 Error; Unknown -> push a Warning (e.g. rule_id "SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-UNKNOWN", message "Certificate '<name>' signature algorithm ref '<sig_ref>' cannot be resolved/classified; unable to verify against the CNSA 2.0 allowlist"); Approved -> nothing. In check_nist_pqc (crypto.rs:579-585) add an AlgorithmClass::Unknown arm that pushes an analogous Warning (e.g. "SBOM-PQC-CERT-UNKNOWN"). Keep the crypto_assets_evaluated increment for parity with the algorithm branch (Unknown algorithms also count but warn); alternatively, only count when the classification is not Unknown so unverifiable certs cannot satisfy the CNSA2-000/PQC-000 inventory gate — either restores "never a silent pass", but the Warning is the minimal, design-consistent fix.

confirmed.title: Protocol assets with nothing evaluable (SSH/QUIC/other, no version, no cipher suites, no refs) count as 'evaluated' and pass both standards vacuously

confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM with a single cryptographic-asset {assetType: protocol, protocolProperties: {type: "ssh"}}: Cnsa2 and NistPqc both return is_compliant=true with ZERO violations (verified).

confirmed.title: CNSA2 TLS gate uses exact string equality with "1.3" — legitimate spellings like "TLSv1.3" or "1.3.0" produce false noncompliance; PQC's lenient parser conversely silently passes unparseable old versions
confirmed.description: check_cnsa2_protocol compares `proto.version.as_deref() != Some("1.3")`, so any non-canonical rendering of TLS 1.3 ("TLSv1.3", "tls1.3", "1.3.0", " 1.3") triggers an SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-001 Error and flips the verdict to noncompliant. Meanwhile check_pqc_protocol uses tls_version_below (line 211), which returns false for unparseable versions, so "TLSv1.0" passes the PQC version gate silently. The two standards should share one normalizing version parser (strip 'TLS'/'v' prefixes, compare (major,minor)), erring to a Warning when unparseable.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM protocol asset {type: "tls", version: "TLSv1.3", cipherSuites: [TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384]} — a fully CNSA-2.0-compliant endpoint — returns Cnsa2 is_compliant=false with 'uses TLS version TLSv1.3, CNSA 2.0 requires TLS 1.3' (verified). Conversely {type: "tls", version: "TLSv1.0"} passes the PQC SP 800-52 version gate.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed end-to-end with the real binary. confirmed.title: Bare "SHA" alias maps to SHA-1 in the declared-family path — algorithmFamily "SHA" + parameterSetIdentifier "384" is reported as broken "SHA-1-384"
confirmed.description: The alias `"SHA-1" | "SHA1" | "SHA" => ("SHA-1", None)` exists for TLS cipher-suite tokens (where bare SHA does mean SHA-1), but classify_token applies the same table to declared algorithmFamily strings. A CBOM that declares the family as "SHA" (meaning the SHA family) with the digest size in parameterSetIdentifier gets classified Broken, and fill_parameter then appends the parameter, producing the self-contradictory label "SHA-1-384" in Error messages. The bare-SHA→SHA-1 mapping should apply only in classify_algorithm_names (cipher-suite/name context), not to the structured family field, or should defer to the parameter set (SHA+384 → SHA-2/384).
confirmed.failure_scenario: CBOM algorithm asset {algorithmFamily: "SHA", parameterSetIdentifier: "384", primitive: hash} — i.e., SHA-384, a CNSA 2.0-approved hash — returns Cnsa2 is_compliant=false with SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005 "uses SHA-1-384, a broken legacy algorithm" and NistPqc is_compliant=false with SBOM-PQC-005 (verified). False noncompliance in both standards.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Verified by code reading and by running the real CLI. src/model/crypto.rs:1117 maps bare "SHA" to ("SHA-1", None) in alias_lookup; classify_algorithm's declared-family path (crypto.rs:1453-1459) applies that same table to CycloneDX algorithmFamily, so {algorithmFamily:"SHA", parameterSetIdentifier:"384"} classifies as family SHA-1 / class Broken, and fill_parameter (1432) attaches "384", yielding label "SHA-1-384" via label() (1079). Reachability confirmed: the CycloneDX parser (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:1994,697) stores algorithmFamily as an unvalidated free string, and src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:40-46 passes it to classify_algorithm; cnsa2_verdict (crypto.rs:92-98) maps Broken to SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005. Running `validate --standard cnsa2` on such a CBOM produced exactly: "NON-COMPLIANT ... 'sha-384-hash' uses SHA-1-384, a broken legacy algorithm not permitted by CNSA 2.0" — a false noncompliance verdict for CNSA 2.0-approved SHA-384 (the PQC standard shares the same classifier and Broken handling). The bare-SHA=SHA-1 comment (crypto.rs:1116) documents only the TLS cipher-suite context, not overriding an explicit parameter set; SHA-1 has no 384-bit variant, so the emitted label is self-contradictory. verdict.suggested_fix: In classify_algorithm (src/model/crypto.rs, declared-family path around line 1453), resolve bare "SHA" using the parameter set before consulting the alias table: if normalize_algo_token(family) == "SHA" and parameter_set trims to one of "224"/"256"/"384"/"512", return family "SHA-2" with that parameter (class Sha2); if it is "1" or "160", return SHA-1. Optionally also guard fill_parameter against appending a parameter to fixed-digest families (SHA-1, MD5) so a contradictory label like "SHA-1-384" can never be rendered.

confirmed.title: Untyped-ML heuristic misfires on HuggingFace-hosted datasets, warning on fully documented AI-BOMs

confirmed.title: Dataset gate (dataset.is_some()) silently drops all BSI-AI Dataset MUST checks for CycloneDX XML AI-BOMs — false pass regression
confirmed.description: df872d1 changed the dataset filter from `c.dataset.is_some() || c.component_type == ComponentType::Data` (at diff base 80818d9, bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs:49) to `c.dataset.is_some()` only. verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. All three factual premises verified in the working tree: (1) ai_shared.rs:77 gates dataset enrollment on `c.dataset.is_some()` alone, while the diff base 80818d9 (bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs) also accepted `component_type == ComponentType::Data`; (2) the CycloneDX XML converter hardcodes `model_card: None, data_components: Vec::new()` (src/parsers/cyclonedx.rs:2320-2323), and Component::dataset is only ever set from CycloneDX JSON data_components (cyclonedx.rs:606) or SPDX3 (spdx3.rs:668) — so no CycloneDX XML component can ever pass the gate, even when the document carries a spec-valid <data> element (verified: the element is silently ignored); (3) reproduced end-to-end with `cargo run -- validate --standard bsi-ai`: equivalent AI-BOM as JSON yields the full Datasets cluster incl. verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. Code inspection and a live run both reproduce the claim exactly.

Evidence:
1. src/reports/sarif.rs:902 `get_sarif_ntia_rules()` declares exactly seven rules (SBOM-NTIA-AUTHOR/NAME/VERSION/SUPPLIER/IDENTIFIER/DEPENDENCY/GENERAL). It declares neither SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP nor SBOM-CRA-GENERAL. `get_sarif_rules_for_standard()` (sarif.rs:892-900) routes NtiaMinimum to this table, so these are the only declared rules for an NTIA run.
2. SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP is a real, reachable rule new to this diff: emitted at src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:444 (severity Error) when `!sbom.document.has_known_timestamp()`, and registry.rs:532-533 maps it to sarif_id "SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP", so the SARIF result carries that ruleId.
3. SBOM-CRA-GENERAL reaches NTIA runs two ways: (a) generic.rs:1059 emits rule_id "SBOM-CRA-GENERAL" directly for the "may be missing bom-ref" Info note in `check_cyclonedx_specific`, which the engine now runs for NTIA (new with d30b23e's fast-path retirement); (b) sarif.rs:686 falls back to "SBOM-CRA-GENERAL" for any unregistered rule_id.
4. Live reproduction: took tests/fixtures/cyclonedx/minimal.cdx.json, removed metadata.timestamp, ran `cargo run -- validate <file> --standard ntia -o sarif`. Output: driver.rules = the 7 declared NTIA ids; results include UNDECLARED SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP (level error — the timestamp gating violation) and UNDECLARED SBOM-CRA-GENERAL (level note — bom-ref check). Even the unmodified minimal.cdx.json (with timestamp) emits the undeclared SBOM-CRA-GENERAL note.
5. verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED (medium severity), with two embellishments in the claim refuted. Verified live: `cargo run -- validate <sbom-without-creators/serial> --standard fda -o sarif` emits results with ruleId SBOM-CRA-GENERAL (creators-empty gating Error from src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:18-27, serial-number warning generic.rs:465, component bom-ref warning) and even SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP, none of which are declared in the FDA run's tool.driver.rules table (get_sarif_fda_rules, src/reports/sarif.rs:977-1090 declares only SBOM-FDA-*). (1) Deleted fast-path (83d9945:src/cli/validate.rs:733-766) warned on orphan_count > 0 && orphan_count < total — any orphan minority was an FDA Warning that drove exit 2 under --fail-on-warning (old validate.rs:147, severity mapping at :426). confirmed.title: CNSA2/PQC report 100% compliant for CBOMs whose only assets have unclassifiable crypto refs (vacuous pass the overhaul was meant to eliminate)
confirmed.description: The crypto rewrite's stated contract (crypto.rs:9-10, registry.rs:877-882, AlgorithmClass::Unknown doc at model/crypto.rs:1035-1037) is 'anything unrecognizable is a Warning, never an implicit pass', and the algorithm path honors it via SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN (crypto.rs:385-408). But the certificate and protocol paths do not: check_cnsa2 increments crypto_assets_evaluated for a certificate at crypto.rs:259 and then only acts on CnsaVerdict::NotApproved at crypto.rs:261, silently dropping CnsaVerdict::Unknown; the PQC certificate arm does the same (crypto.rs:577-585, `problem` is None for Unknown); and both protocols' `record` closures ignore AlgorithmClass::Unknown for cipher-suite/IKEv2/crypto-ref bom-refs (crypto.rs:477-484, 857-869). Because these unverifiable assets still count toward the CNSA2-000/PQC-000 inventory gate, they satisfy the gate while receiving no effective evaluation — exactly the false-pass mode commit 7a1c9c2 was written to close, and the classify_bom_ref doc comment (crypto.rs:53) explicitly claims opaque refs 'classify as Unknown rather than silently passing checks'. The mod.rs tests cover opaque refs that RESOLVE to a classifiable component and unresolvable refs with recognizable name tokens (mod.rs:2075, 2104), but not the unrecognizable-ref case.
confirmed.failure_scenario: VERIFIED via CLI: a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM whose only crypto asset is a certificate with `certificateProperties.signatureAlgorithmRef: "sig-algo-42"` (no matching component, no recognizable token) -> `sbom-tools validate <file> --standard cnsa2 --summary` prints {"compliant":true,"score":100,"errors":0,"warnings":0} and exits 0; same for --standard pqc. Also VERIFIED: a CBOM whose only asset is an IKEv2 protocol with four opaque transform refs (encr/prf/integ/ke = "transform-encr-7" etc.) -> compliant:true score:100 under BOTH cnsa2 and pqc. An identical unverifiable ALGORITHM asset would instead produce an ALG-UNKNOWN Warning (exit 2 with --fail-on-warning), so the cert/protocol paths hand out a false CNSA 2.0 / PQC-readiness attestation for inventories the tool never actually verified.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Code inspection: src/quality/compliance/crypto.rs:259 counts a certificate toward the CNSA2-000 inventory gate whenever signature_algorithm_ref exists, but line 261 only matches CnsaVerdict::NotApproved, silently dropping CnsaVerdict::Unknown (no Warning arm, unlike the algorithm path's SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN at lines 385-408). The PQC certificate arm (lines 577-585) counts the asset then maps AlgorithmClass::Unknown to problem=None. Both protocols' record closures (CNSA2 lines 477-484, PQC lines 857-869) ignore AlgorithmClass::Unknown, and an IKEv2 protocol is also outside the TLS/SSL version gates, so a protocol with only opaque transform refs counts as 'evaluated' (lines 280, 605) while receiving no effective check. Reproduced via CLI on HEAD (b730c80): a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM whose sole asset is a certificate with signatureAlgorithmRef "sig-algo-42" (unresolvable, no recognizable token) and a second fixture whose sole asset is an IKEv2 protocol with four opaque transform refs both yield {"compliant":true,"score":100,"errors":0,"warnings":0} exit 0 under both `sbom-tools validate --standard cnsa2 --summary` and `--standard pqc --summary`. This contradicts the module's stated contract in three places (crypto.rs:9-10 'anything unrecognizable is a Warning, never an implicit pass'; crypto.rs:53 opaque refs 'classify as Unknown rather than silently passing checks'; gate comments at 235-236 and 550-553 'only assets that receive a substantive check are counted'), so it is a genuine defect of the P0 work, not a deliberate documented decision. Severity high: false CNSA 2.0 / PQC-readiness compliance verdict.
verdict.suggested_fix: Honor the Unknown classification on the certificate and protocol paths, mirroring the algorithm path: (1) crypto.rs:261 — match cnsa2_verdict exhaustively and add a CnsaVerdict::Unknown arm emitting a Warning (e.g. rule SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-UNKNOWN: "Certificate '<name>' signature algorithm ref '<sig_ref>' cannot be classified; unable to verify against the CNSA 2.0 allowlist"). (2) crypto.rs:579-585 — add an AlgorithmClass::Unknown arm producing a Warning (SBOM-PQC-CERT-UNKNOWN) instead of problem=None. (3) In both check_cnsa2_protocol and check_pqc_protocol, have the record closures also collect refs/names that classify as AlgorithmClass::Unknown into a separate `unverifiable` list, and after processing emit one Warning per protocol asset (e.g. SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-UNKNOWN / SBOM-PQC-PROTO-UNKNOWN) listing the unclassifiable refs; optionally also classify unresolvable cipher-suite algorithm refs via classify_bom_ref (crypto.rs:491, 874) instead of skipping them when resolve_component returns None. Alternatively (weaker but minimal), stop incrementing crypto_assets_evaluated for assets whose every classification came back Unknown so they cannot satisfy the CNSA2-000/PQC-000 gate — but the Warning approach matches the documented contract and the existing ALG-UNKNOWN precedent.
