confirmed.failure_scenario: VERIFIED via CLI: `sbom-tools validate tests/fixtures/cyclonedx/cbom-weak-crypto.cdx.json --standard cnsa2 -o sarif` produces a run where tool.driver.rules has 38 entries (SBOM-AIACT-*, SBOM-BSIAI-*, SBOM-CRA-*, SBOM-BSI-*) and results reference ruleIds SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-001/005/006, SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-001, SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-001/002 — 100% of referenced ruleIds are absent from the catalogue. GitHub code scanning ingests these results without rule metadata (no name, no shortDescription, no defaultConfiguration, no helpUri — note rule_help_uri's 'SBOM-CNSA-' prefix at sarif.rs:730 would not match 'SBOM-CNSA2-' anyway), and the uploaded rules list advertises 38 rules that can never fire in that run.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by reading the code and reproducing via the real CLI. (1) src/reports/sarif.rs:892-899: get_sarif_rules_for_standard has dedicated arms only for NtiaMinimum/FdaMedicalDevice/NistSsdf/Eo14028; ComplianceLevel::Cnsa2 and ::NistPqc hit the `_ => get_sarif_compliance_rules()` wildcard. (2) get_sarif_compliance_rules (sarif.rs:1294 onward) contains exactly 38 rules — 16 SBOM-CRA-*, 7 SBOM-BSI-TR-03183-*, 7 SBOM-AIACT-*, 8 SBOM-BSIAI-* — and zero SBOM-CNSA2-*/SBOM-PQC-* entries (grep for "SBOM-CNSA"/"SBOM-PQC" in sarif.rs hits only the rule_help_uri prefixes at lines 728/730). (3) Reproduced: `cargo run --quiet -- validate tests/fixtures/cyclonedx/cbom-weak-crypto.cdx.json --standard cnsa2 -o sarif` yields tool.driver.rules with 38 entries (none CNSA/PQC) while results reference SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-001/005/006, SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-001, SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-001/002 — 6 of 6 result ruleIds undeclared. Same for `--standard nist-pqc` on cbom-pqc-transition.cdx.json: SBOM-PQC-001/009/010, SBOM-PQC-CERT-001, SBOM-PQC-PROTO-002 — 5 of 5 undeclared. (4) The helpUri sub-claim also holds: rule_help_uri at sarif.rs:730 tests starts_with("SBOM-CNSA-"), which "SBOM-CNSA2-..." does not satisfy (the char after "SBOM-CNSA" is '2', not '-'), so even once catalogued, CNSA2 rules would get no helpUri; the SBOM-PQC- prefix at sarif.rs:728 does match. (5) The registry at src/quality/compliance/registry.rs:861-862 does register SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-005 etc. as sarif_id, and the parallel AI cluster in the same P0 diff DID extend get_sarif_compliance_rules with its new rules (SBOM-AIACT-ANNEX-IV-2C, SBOM-AIACT-UNTYPED-ML, SBOM-BSIAI-UNTYPED-ML present in the catalogue), so the omission for the crypto cluster is an inconsistency, not a deliberate decision. Severity: broken SARIF output contract — every result in a cnsa2/pqc run references an undeclared ruleId, so consumers like GitHub code scanning get no rule metadata (name, shortDescription, defaultConfiguration, helpUri), while 38 irrelevant CRA/BSI/AI rules are advertised.
verdict.suggested_fix: In src/reports/sarif.rs: (a) add dedicated arms in get_sarif_rules_for_standard (lines 893-898): `ComplianceLevel::Cnsa2 => get_sarif_cnsa2_rules(), ComplianceLevel::NistPqc => get_sarif_pqc_rules(),` and implement those two functions listing the rule ids the crypto engine actually emits — CNSA2: SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-001..008, SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-UNKNOWN, SBOM-CNSA2-PROTO-001/002, SBOM-CNSA2-CERT-001; PQC: SBOM-PQC-001..010, SBOM-PQC-PROTO-001/002, SBOM-PQC-CERT-001 — ideally generated from the sarif_id/RuleMeta table in src/quality/compliance/registry.rs (which already claims to mirror the SARIF catalogue) so the two cannot drift again. (b) fix rule_help_uri at sarif.rs:730 to `rule_id.starts_with("SBOM-CNSA2-") || rule_id.starts_with("SBOM-CNSA-")` so CNSA2 rules resolve the CNSA 2.0 advisory URL. Then refresh the golden SARIF snapshot and add an invariant test asserting every result.ruleId in a cnsa2/pqc run appears in tool.driver.rules.

confirmed.title: FDA SARIF runs now emit SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP results that are missing from the FDA per-standard rule catalogue
confirmed.description: Cluster 1/3 extended the NTIA timestamp gate to FdaMedicalDevice (generic.rs:425-446) but kept rule_id "SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP". The FDA SARIF catalogue get_sarif_fda_rules (sarif.rs:978-1090) contains only SBOM-FDA-* rules, so the new FDA timestamp Error references a ruleId undeclared in the run's catalogue (SBOM-CRA-GENERAL from the creator check at generic.rs:18-42 has the same problem, but that path predates this branch — the timestamp emission is new). Same root cause as the CNSA2 catalogue gap: per-standard catalogues were not reconciled with the cross-standard rule ids the engine now emits under that standard.
confirmed.failure_scenario: VERIFIED via CLI: `sbom-tools validate <cyclonedx-without-metadata.timestamp> --standard fda -o sarif` emits results with ruleIds ['SBOM-CRA-GENERAL', 'SBOM-FDA-GENERAL', 'SBOM-FDA-HASH', 'SBOM-FDA-SUPPLIER', 'SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT', 'SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP'] of which SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP and SBOM-CRA-GENERAL are absent from tool.driver.rules; code-scanning consumers get an FDA gating Error with no rule metadata, and dedup/grouping by rule falls outside the advertised FDA rule set.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. (1) Code: the P0 diff added ComplianceLevel::FdaMedicalDevice to the timestamp gate at src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:425-447 (rule_id "SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP" at generic.rs:444); at base 80818d9 the gate matched only NtiaMinimum | Comprehensive, so the FDA-level emission is new to this branch. The registry maps it 1:1 to sarif_id "SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP" (src/quality/compliance/registry.rs:532-533), and generate_compliance_sarif (src/reports/sarif.rs:560-561) builds tool.driver.rules from the static per-standard catalogue via get_sarif_rules_for_standard -> get_sarif_fda_rules (src/reports/sarif.rs:895, 977-1090), which contains only SBOM-FDA-* ids — no SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP and no SBOM-CRA-GENERAL. There is no reconciliation step that appends descriptors for emitted-but-undeclared rule ids. (2) Reproduced end-to-end via the real CLI: `cargo run -- validate <cyclonedx-without-metadata.timestamp> --standard fda -o sarif` produced declared rules = 11 SBOM-FDA-* ids, emitted ruleIds = [SBOM-CRA-GENERAL, SBOM-FDA-GENERAL, SBOM-FDA-HASH, SBOM-FDA-IDENTIFIER, SBOM-FDA-SUPPLIER, SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT, SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP]; the SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP result is level "error" (an FDA gating violation) with no rule descriptor in the run. Not a deliberate decision — nothing in the diff or comments acknowledges the catalogue gap, and the same cluster added FDA-specific requirement text ("FDA (NTIA baseline): Timestamp") showing FDA presentation was considered but the SARIF catalogue was not reconciled. Note the same regression also applies to --standard ntia after cluster 3's fast-path retirement: get_sarif_ntia_rules (sarif.rs:902-975) also lacks SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP. Severity medium: SARIF 2.1.0 tolerates results whose ruleId has no descriptor, so output is not invalid, but code-scanning consumers get a gating Error with no metadata/help and rule-based grouping falls outside the advertised per-standard rule set (misleading output / contract deviation), matching the claim.
verdict.suggested_fix: Reconcile the declared catalogue with emitted results in src/reports/sarif.rs: in generate_compliance_sarif (and generate_multi_compliance_sarif), after building the per-standard rules, scan the SarifResults and append a SarifRule (id/name/short_description from registry rule_meta, default level from the violation severity) for any emitted sarif ruleId not already declared, deduplicating by id. This closes both the new SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP gap under FDA/NTIA and the pre-existing SBOM-CRA-GENERAL gap in one place. Minimal alternative: add an SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP SarifRule entry to get_sarif_fda_rules() and get_sarif_ntia_rules(), plus SBOM-CRA-GENERAL to get_sarif_fda_rules().

lows.title: manufacturer_scope_components ignores co-described root products once a primary is set, dropping legitimate manufacturer evidence in multi-DESCRIBES SPDX documents
lows.description: When primary_component_id is set the scope is exactly vec![primary]. The SPDX parser sets the primary to the FIRST 'DOCUMENT DESCRIBES X' relationship only (src/parsers/spdx.rs:777-798), and document-level DESCRIBES edges are dropped (SPDXRef-DOCUMENT is not in id_map, spdx.rs:840-852), so other described products are neither primary nor reachable via the root-fallback branch. A multi-product SPDX document (DOCUMENT DESCRIBES product-A and product-B) that carries the manufacturer's security-contact/advisories externalRef on product-B (or on both products but parsed with B second) has that evidence ignored by every manufacturer-scoped gate: CRA Art. 13(6)/13(7) (generic.rs:139-176, 265-297), EO 14028 Sec 4(g) (eo14028.rs:191), steward Art. 24 (cra.rs:975). Note also that which package is 'first described' depends on relationship order in the file, making the verdict order-sensitive for such documents.
lows.failure_scenario: SPDX monorepo document describing two products where the CVD/advisories externalRef sits on the second-described product → CRA Phase 2 validate emits the Art. 13(6)/13(7) warnings (and EO 4(g)) despite the manufacturer evidence being present on a document-described root product; reordering the DESCRIBES relationships changes the result.

lows.title: FDA vulnerability warning counts (component, vulnerability) pairs, inflating critical/high counts when one CVE affects multiple components
lows.description: The new FDA check (parity moved from the retired validate fast-path in d30b23e) counts sbom.all_vulnerabilities(), which flat-maps per-component vulnerability refs (src/model/sbom.rs:221-226). A CycloneDX vulnerability whose 'affects' lists N components is attached to each of them by apply_vulnerability, so a single critical CVE affecting 5 components is reported as '5 critical'. The warning's trigger (>=1) is unaffected, but the counts in the message 'SBOM contains {critical} critical and {high} high severity vulnerabilities' overstate the vulnerability population and will not match `sbom-tools view` or external scanner counts. Dedup by vuln.id before counting.
lows.failure_scenario: CycloneDX SBOM with one critical vulnerability entry whose affects[] lists 5 bom-refs → `validate --standard fda` warns 'SBOM contains 5 critical and 0 high severity vulnerabilities', misreporting a single CVE as five.

lows.title: Vendor-hash gate pairs phase-derived Error severity with the class-threshold message, misattributing why it is an Error
lows.description: In the (Some(phase), Some(class)) combination (cra.rs:362-367), when the phase gate outranks the class gate the code emits (phase severity, class message). Reachable when CraPhase2 coverage <50% (phase Error) with an explicit Default or Important-1 class (class severity Warning). Verified via CLI: 4/10 vendor hashes + `--cra-product-class important-1` under `--standard cra` yields 'Error | ... 40% ... below 80% threshold for product class Important-1'. Per the calibration table (mod.rs:774-776) Important-1's 80% threshold is Warning-severity; the Error actually comes from the Phase-2 50% floor, which the message never mentions. At 55% coverage the identical message text appears at Warning.
lows.failure_scenario: An auditor reading the Phase-2 report for an Important-1 product concludes the class's 80% threshold is Error-gated (it is Warning-gated) and cannot tell from the message which threshold (50% phase floor vs 80% class bar) caused the Error; the same message string flips between Error and Warning across coverage values with no textual difference.

lows.title: Conformity summary 'Target of Evaluation reference' row is satisfied by any EUCC field, including ones that are not a ToE
lows.description: Both EUCC-route evidence rows ('EUCC / Common Criteria certificate' at cra.rs:103-107 and 'Target of Evaluation reference' at cra.rs:108-113) key on the single aggregate eucc_present boolean (cra.rs:50-61). A sidecar carrying only eucc_itsef_identifier or eucc_valid_until — with eucc_target_of_evaluation absent — marks the ToE row satisfied. The sidecar has a dedicated eucc_target_of_evaluation field the row could key on. Verified via CLI: sidecar with only euccValidUntil shows 'Target of Evaluation reference => satisfied: True' in the Annex VIII summary. Also the rows' detail text still claims satisfaction requires 'Certification external ref whose URL references EUCC or common-criteria', which is stale now that sidecar fields count.
lows.failure_scenario: A notified-body checklist generated from the conformity summary asserts the ToE reference is present when the sidecar only names the evaluating lab (ITSEF) or a validity date; the Annex VIII dossier row is affirmatively wrong rather than flagged as a gap.

lows.title: NIST sigAlgs OIDs 32–34 (HashML-DSA-44/65/87-with-SHA512) misclassified as SLH-DSA
lows.description: classify_oid maps `20..=35` under 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3 to SLH-DSA, but per the NIST CSOR registry only 20–31 are SLH-DSA parameter sets; 32/33/34 are id-hash-ml-dsa-44/65/87-with-sha512 (pre-hash ML-DSA, FIPS 204). A CBOM declaring HashML-DSA-87 by OID gets the Error "uses SLH-DSA, which is NIST-approved (FIPS 205) but not part of CNSA 2.0" (verified) — wrong family, wrong FIPS citation, and arguably the wrong CNSA verdict for the ML-DSA-87 pre-hash variant. PQC-009's informational note likewise cites the wrong standard.
lows.failure_scenario: CBOM algorithm asset with oid "2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.34" (HashML-DSA-87): CNSA2 output claims the component uses SLH-DSA and fails it under SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-008; reports mislabel the algorithm family in SARIF/report output.

lows.title: Over-generic name tokens ("SEED", "EC"/"ECC") fire on incidental words in name-only fallback — 'seed-expander' flagged as the SEED block cipher
lows.description: classify_algorithm_names matches the aliases "SEED" (Korean block cipher) and "EC"/"ECC" as standalone word tokens. In the guarded name fallback (algorithm assets without family/OID) and the raw-ref-string fallback in classify_bom_ref, common non-crypto words collide: a DRBG seed utility named "seed-expander", refs containing "seed", or tokens like "ec2" (trailing-digit split yields EC+2 → ClassicalQuantumVulnerable). Empirically 'seed-expander' produces SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-008 Error "uses SEED, which is not a CNSA 2.0 approved algorithm" → false noncompliance.
lows.failure_scenario: CBOM algorithm asset named "seed-expander" with no algorithmFamily/OID: Cnsa2 returns is_compliant=false with 'uses SEED' (verified). Similarly an IKEv2 transform ref string containing "ec2" or "seed" is recorded as a quantum-vulnerable/non-approved offender.

lows.title: SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-007 blanket 'quantum level 5 required' fires on CNSA-approved LMS/XMSS/HSS assets that honestly declare a lower NIST category
lows.description: check_cnsa2_algorithm errors on any non-symmetric/hash primitive with declared nistQuantumSecurityLevel < 5, before and independent of the allowlist verdict. The SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signatures are explicitly Approved by cnsa2_verdict (line 179) — they are the CNSA 2.0-mandated firmware-signing algorithms — yet several approved parameter sets (e.g., SHA-256/192 variants) sit below NIST category 5, so an accurately-documented LMS asset fails CNSA 2.0. Verified: {algorithmFamily: LMS, primitive: signature, nistQuantumSecurityLevel: 2} → is_compliant=false via SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-007 while the allowlist simultaneously approves it. The level gate should exempt assets whose classification verdict is Approved (or at least the PostQuantum Lms/Xmss/Hss kinds).
lows.failure_scenario: CBOM with one LMS firmware-signing asset declaring an honest quantum security category < 5: CNSA2 verdict is noncompliant ('quantum level 2 < 5, CNSA 2.0 requires Level 5') even though LMS is on the CNSA 2.0 allowlist, penalizing exactly the algorithm CNSA 2.0 mandates for that use case.

lows.title: Documented exit-code/output contract changes for validate --standard ntia/fda (intended but breaking)
lows.description: Contract changes from retiring the fast-paths onto the engine, verified by live runs: (1) NTIA missing supplier/version/identifier were fast-path Warnings, engine emits Errors — `validate minimal.cdx.json --standard ntia` now exits 1 (was 0), and `view --validate-ntia` flips 'NTIA Validation: PASSED' to 'FAILED' listing per-component errors on the same fixture; print_ntia_validation (validate.rs:327) also drops Info-level findings silently and no longer returns Result. (2) FDA gains a new gating Error for missing/epoch timestamps (SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP) and a new SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT warning when no support-lifecycle evidence exists (FD&C 524B, generic.rs:403), so previously-passing FDA SBOMs can now exit 1/2. (3) FDA aggregate messages ('X/N components missing version information') became per-component violations — error counts inflate and message-text parsers break. (4) Placeholder values (NOASSERTION/NONE) now count as missing via known_value gates, further tightening both standards. These match the audit's intent but are externally visible behavior changes that release notes/CI consumers must account for.
lows.failure_scenario: A CI job running `sbom-tools validate app.cdx.json --standard ntia` that previously treated missing suppliers as non-gating (exit 0) hard-fails with exit 1 after upgrade with no flag to restore the old severity mapping; scripts parsing the old 'X/N components missing ...' FDA aggregate messages or the old NTIA issue strings ('Component missing name') no longer match.

lows.title: Stale registry comments and dead rule keys left from removed fast-path; declared severities contradict emitted
lows.description: registry.rs:587 and :620 still document SBOM-FDA-CREATOR/NAMESPACE/DEPENDENCY and the NTIA block as 'rules emitted by the `validate` NTIA/FDA fast-path (`cli::validate`), which builds violations directly' — that code was deleted in d30b23e; SBOM-FDA-CREATOR, SBOM-FDA-NAMESPACE, and SBOM-FDA-DEPENDENCY now have no emit site anywhere (grep-verified). Relatedly, the SARIF NTIA table declares SBOM-NTIA-VERSION and SBOM-NTIA-IDENTIFIER with defaultConfiguration.level 'warning' (sarif.rs:931, :951) and registry.rs:635 keeps SBOM-NTIA-IDENTIFIER default_severity Warning, while the engine now emits both as Errors — per-result level overrides make this cosmetic, but the declared defaults misrepresent the rules' actual gating behavior.
lows.failure_scenario: A developer adding a new FDA check reads the registry comment, concludes cli::validate still builds FDA violations directly, and patches the deleted path's semantics; a SARIF consumer inspecting the NTIA driver rules concludes missing identifiers are non-gating warnings when they in fact produce exit-code-1 errors.

lows.title: Registry and SARIF catalogue declare SBOM-NTIA-IDENTIFIER default severity Warning, but the new NTIA identifier gate always emits Error
lows.description: The new NTIA 'Other Unique Identifiers' gate (generic.rs:568-601, NtiaMinimum included in the Error-severity arm at generic.rs:582-592; asserted as Error by mod.rs test ntia_gates_on_missing_identifier) emits ViolationSeverity::Error unconditionally, but the rule registry entry added in the same cluster records default_severity: Warning (registry.rs:633-638), and the NTIA SARIF catalogue keeps defaultConfiguration.level = warning with the stale description 'PURL/CPE/SWID' (sarif.rs:944-953, missing SWHID which the check now accepts). The registry's own doc says the default 'is surfaced in the SARIF rule catalogue' — both surfaces now contradict every actual result.
lows.failure_scenario: A component without PURL/CPE/SWHID/SWID under `validate --standard ntia -o sarif` produces a result with level 'error' under rule SBOM-NTIA-IDENTIFIER whose declared defaultConfiguration is 'warning'; code-scanning UIs and policy engines keying off the rule's default severity (e.g. 'fail only on rules whose default is error') misclassify a gating NTIA element as advisory.

lows.title: CNSA2 TLS version gate uses exact string equality with "1.3" while the PQC gate in the same file parses versions numerically
lows.description: check_cnsa2_protocol flags any TLS/DTLS protocol whose version string is not exactly "1.3" (crypto.rs:436-456), whereas check_pqc_protocol parses the version numerically via tls_version_below (crypto.rs:211-218, 819-822) and treats unparseable versions as unverifiable. The two standards in the same module therefore disagree on the same input: version "1.3.0", "TLSv1.3" or "1.3 " (trailing space survives because as_deref() is compared without trim) is a hard CNSA2-PROTO-001 Error but passes the PQC version gate silently.
lows.failure_scenario: A CBOM protocol asset with protocolProperties {type: "tls", version: "1.3.0"} -> `validate --standard cnsa2` reports Error 'uses TLS version 1.3.0, CNSA 2.0 requires TLS 1.3' and flips the verdict to NON-COMPLIANT (exit 1) for a TLS 1.3 endpoint; the same SBOM passes the PQC version gate, so multi-standard output shows contradictory protocol-version verdicts for one asset.

lows.title: Registry-exhaustiveness test only exercises the empty SBOM despite claiming 'a representative fixture set'; unregistered rule ids on non-empty SBOMs silently rebucket to SBOM-CRA-GENERAL in SARIF
lows.description: every_emitted_violation_has_a_registered_rule_id (mod.rs:2241-2258) documents 'across all compliance levels and a representative fixture set' but checks only NormalizedSbom::default(). An empty SBOM cannot reach any of the ~24 crypto rule ids (they require Cryptographic components), most AI rule ids, or the per-component gates, so the merge's main cross-cluster invariant — every new rule id from the three parallel branches being registered — is not actually enforced by this test; coverage instead depends on scattered per-module tests. The failure mode it should guard is silent: compliance_results_to_sarif falls back to sarif_rule_id "SBOM-CRA-GENERAL" for unregistered keys (src/reports/sarif.rs:685-686), so a future unregistered id emitted only on non-trivial SBOMs would ship rebucketed under a CRA rule with generic remediation and no test failure.
lows.failure_scenario: Add a new check that emits rule_id "SBOM-CNSA2-ALG-009" (or typo an existing id) for a classified algorithm asset: the full 1731-test suite stays green because no test feeds a Cryptographic component through the registry-exhaustiveness gate, and `validate --standard cnsa2 -o sarif` reports the finding as ruleId SBOM-CRA-GENERAL — a CNSA violation surfaced to code scanning as a generic CRA documentation issue.

refuted.reason: The mechanical behavior is as the reviewer describes: with no primary_component_id and no edges, manufacturer_scope_components (src/quality/compliance/shared.rs:14-31) returns every component, so a third-party component's Advisories/Support refs suppress the SBOM-CRA-ART-13-6-CONTACT and SBOM-CRA-AR
